chunks: Nasr ibn Qabus said: I said to Abu al-Hasan (the preceding Imam, peace be upon him), 'It has reached me that someone came to your father asking for help with his need, but he was told that he was in i'tikaf. So, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came and mentioned this to him. He said, 'Do you not know that going to help a believer is better than two consecutive months of i'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque, fasting during them?' Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) added, 'And better than i'tikaf for the whole lifetime.'

key_terms.اعْتِكَاف: I'tikaf (spiritual retreat/confinement in a mosque for worship)
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدُ الْحَرَام: Al-Masjid al-Haram (The Sacred Mosque in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of helping a believer compared to i'tikaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), preferred helping a believer in need over two months of continuous i'tikaf (spiritual retreat) in the Sacred Mosque. He further emphasized that assisting a believer is superior even to performing i'tikaf for one's entire life, highlighting the high value of social support and relieving distress.
